Commuter/daily rider? Schwinn Varsity, I think early '70s (the decades overlap on the serials which can make a bit of trouble identifying). Suntour AR components. I bought it last month for $15, complete with alloy fenders. I can't get the fucking Kenda tire to seat evenly all the way across, but at least it's down to one point where it's still stuck along the ridge instead of seated on the rim, instead of the motherfucking three that were on there when I got it (jesus that was the ride from hell).

That aside, it's actually a pretty okay commuter, I even managed an 18.5 MPH average commute on it once, complete with a backpack, though I was exhausted when I got in. It came with a broken speedometer (seriously, what were the speedo cables made with, spaghetti? They are always broken. This one didn't even last 80 miles, though the mechanism itself works fine.) The tires are fairly recent, so they're still solid, too. The rims, despite being steel, somehow actually do okay in wet weather. I can't explain it- every other steel rim I've ever had has been utter dogshit in wet weather, but these are just fine, they even outperformed the alloys (with admittedly old brake pads) on a late '80s Schwinn. I can't explain it, but I guess 'hey, if it works, don't question it.' The frame's oversized, so at the weld points it droops a bit because that's just how they made the taller ElectroForged frames. The forged bladed fork is weird but works well enough, and feels really solid. The only downside is the new chain keeps popping for reasons I don't understand. I did put a 7sp master link on it, but I thought 5/6/7 spd. chains were all pretty interchangeable. Regardless, I may swap the stock freewheel off if that keeps up, because it's obnoxious to deal with.

I'm also rebuilding a Schwinn Prelude which is giving me lots of mechanical trouble (I opened the BB to find it was missing a ball bearing. Like, no sign of it, just straight up missing. 11 balls on one side, 10 on the other. What? How? Just...I... how?) and a really slick Schwinn Tempo. Columbus tubing on both.

So I have a pair of among Schwinn's lightest and heaviest bikes ever made, even if the Varsity doesn't have that Huret-with-bash-guard monstrosity rear derailleur, or full steel fenders, it's still a tank.
